cards.front: Recall a key point about Finishing Techniques
cards.back: Metal finishes - functional: galvanising (zinc coating prevents rust), anodising (thickened aluminium oxide layer - harder, can be dyed), plating (chromium/nickel for hardness). Decorative: powder coating (baked polymer - durable, many colours), painting (versatile but less durable).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Finishing Techniques
cards.back: Timber finishes - functional: preservative (prevents rot), fire retardant. Decorative: varnish (clear, highlights grain, waterproof), oil (penetrates wood, natural), wax (soft sheen, less durable), paint (opaque, hides grain), stain (changes colour, shows grain).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Finishing Techniques
cards.back: Polymer finishes - self-finishing (coloured in the mould). Surface: printing (pad, screen, hot-foil), texturing (etched mould surfaces), vacuum metallising.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Finishing Techniques
cards.back: Textile finishes - functional: waterproofing (DWR coating), flame retardancy, stain resistance. Decorative: dyeing, printing, embroidery, applique.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Finishing Techniques
cards.back: Finishing purpose: protection (corrosion, UV, abrasion, moisture), identification (branding, safety warnings), aesthetics (colour, texture, sheen).

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: For finishing questions: 1) Identify the material, 2) State requirements, 3) Propose an appropriate finish, 4) Explain how it works, 5) Justify the choice.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Painting is always the best finish because it gives the most colour options and covers any surface. Correct: Paint is versatile but has limitations: it chips and scratches easily, hides the material beneath, requires surface preparation and regular maintenance.
